newsitem.title: INDIA: India state gets $150 mln World Bank disaster aid.
newsitem.headline: India state gets $150 mln World Bank disaster aid.

text.p: The World Bank said on Wednesday it will provide $150 million as aid to the southern Indian state of Andhra Pradesh to help it recover from last year's devastating cyclone and cope with future disasters.

"The Bank will provide $100 million equivalent credit through the International Development Association (IDA), the bank's concessionary lending affiliate, and a $50 million loan," the bank said in a statement.

The southern state, India's fifth largest in area and fourth most populous, has a geographic location and topography that make it vulnerable to tropical storms, storm surge and seasonal monsoon floods, the statement said.

The aid would help the state implement a hazard management system to prevent and mitigate the damage caused by cyclones, floods and drought; rebuild public infrastructure and make them withstand future disasters; and enhance cyclone warning capacity, the statement said.

More than 1,000 people died last November in cyclone-related events in Andhra Pradesh, and some reports said the death toll may have reached 2,000. The state government estimated economic losses arising out of the cycline at $1.5 billion.
